title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page completes the theorem stated at the end of p.21. Setting: X is a smooth projective connected curve of genus g ≥ 2. A projective connection (in modern terms an sl2- or PGL2-oper) gives a principal H-bundle with H = PGL(2), together with a flat connection.

On the previous page Grothendieck showed that the structure group cannot be reduced to a proper subgroup.
- **Borel.** Write the rank-2 bundle as E ≃ F⊗L with det E ≃ det F⊗L^2. Then deg L = g−1, and the composite ω^{-1} → E → L must vanish for degree reasons. This would force L ≅ O_X, which is absurd.
- **Normalizer of a maximal torus.** Pass to the étale double cover, which reduces to the torus case and hence to the Borel case. The cover still has genus ≥ 2.

This page says: when k = ℂ, the statement means that the monodromy homomorphism π1(X^an, x) → H(ℂ) = PGL2(ℂ) has Zariski-dense image in H_ℂ.

The implicit argument runs as follows.
- Let H' be the Zariski closure of the monodromy group.
- By Riemann–Hilbert (and GAGA for the algebraicity of the flat bundle), the flat H-bundle admits a horizontal reduction to H'.
- The theorem forbids any reduction to a proper closed subgroup, so H' = H.
- Equivalently, the differential Galois group of the projective connection is all of PGL2.

The classification of proper algebraic subgroups of PGL2 justifies the two cases treated on p.21.
- Those with Borel identity component are contained in a Borel.
- Those with toral identity component lie in a torus normalizer.
- Finite ones (cyclic, dihedral, A4, S4, A5) are handled by the étale-cover trick: the cover has genus ≥ 2 and trivial monodromy, so the bundle reduces to {1} ⊂ Borel, which contradicts the degree argument.

The purpose within the manuscript is to show that the monodromy of every projective structure, in particular the uniformizing one, is 'big' (non-elementary). This feeds the uniformization theme of cote 159.
errors: The previous-page theorem must be read as 'no horizontal reduction (compatible with the connection)' for the equivalence with Zariski density to hold. A mere reduction of the underlying bundle is a stronger claim, and that is what the degree argument actually proves, so this is fine, but the equivalence direction used here needs horizontality.

The finite-subgroup case is not explicitly treated, though the étale-cover argument covers it. The page also tacitly uses characteristic 0 (Riemann–Hilbert/GAGA) and that étale covers of a genus ≥ 2 curve keep genus ≥ 2, and it does not detail the step from 'no proper reduction' to 'Zariski dense'. These are minor gaps, not errors.

ideas.what: Monodromy of any projective connection (projective structure) on a compact Riemann surface of genus ≥ 2 has Zariski-dense image in PGL2(ℂ), i.e. it is non-elementary.
ideas.modern_name: Non-elementary / Zariski-dense monodromy of complex projective structures (PGL2-opers); differential Galois group of an oper is the full group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967, irreducibility of monodromy of projective structures); Gallo–Kapovich–Marden (2000, characterization of such monodromy as non-elementary); oper version folklore (Beilinson–Drinfeld)

ideas.what: Algebraic proof via the impossibility of reducing the oper bundle to a Borel (degree of the Hodge line bundle = g−1 ≠ 0), plus étale covers for torus normalizers and finite groups. This is a characteristic-free-looking algebraic formulation over a general field k.
ideas.modern_name: Oper bundles admit no reduction to a proper parabolic / irreducibility of opers via Hodge filtration degree
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in oper literature (Beilinson–Drinfeld; also Katz-style differential Galois arguments)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean algebraic proof of a known fact (Zariski density / non-elementarity of monodromy of projective structures in genus ≥ 2), established by Gunning and others. It is interesting only as evidence of Grothendieck's own algebraic treatment of projective connections; nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'X^{\circ}' is most likely 'X^{an}' (analytic space associated to X); the superscript in the image reads as 'an' with a hook.
'à une image Zariski-dense' should read 'a une image Zariski-dense' (verb avoir).
